clue.text: Soldiers surrender, getting run through

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a regiment of British Army soldiers
to capitulate is to surrender

explanation.surface: Troops give themselves up and are then bayoneted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run through' looks like a stabbing, but it means go over again briefly, as in summing up.
explanation.definitionFit: To run through a story is to summarise its main points again, a synonym.

clue.text: Fare when instrument's carried by rail reduced by 25%

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, so the instrument goes within the shortened rail
reduced means cut down, and 'by 25%' says one of the four letters goes, the last

parts.note: a viol is an early bowed string instrument

explanation.surface: Food served on a train when a musician boards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like a ticket price on the railway, but it means food; a quarter of a four-letter word is one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare means food served, and this pasta dish is an example.

clue.text: Name a pupil in class

indicators.note: in places the letters inside the abbreviation for class

parts.note: CL is an abbreviation for class
L stands for learner, a pupil driver

explanation.surface: A teacher reads out a child's name in the classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' suggests a schoolchild; here it is a learner driver, L.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone something is to give them a name, a synonym.

clue.text: Snack vice cop unwisely swallowed

indicators.note: swallowed means taken inside, so the vice goes round the rearranged policeman

parts.note: pornography is a vice in the sense of immoral trade

indicators.note: unwisely means foolishly, done the wrong way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vice squad officer gulped down a bite to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vice cop' reads as one officer of the vice squad, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Popped maize kernels are a common cinema snack.

clue.text: Proposition from her to me?

indicators.note: from here means formed out of, so the answer is made from the letters of the words given

explanation.surface: A suggestion passed from one woman to me.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks that 'from' signals letters made from HER TO ME.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a theorem is a proposition to be proved from axioms.

clue.text: Drinks by mistake left unfinished

indicators.note: left unfinished means without its end, so the last letter of the mistake is dropped

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: Accidentally, someone leaves their drinks half-finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat drinks by lapping, so laps is a verb meaning drinks.

clue.text: Shelter occupied by old bishop in downpour

indicators.note: occupied by means having someone inside, so the old bishop goes into the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a shelter
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: An elderly bishop stays in a tent during heavy rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent rush of water, and here a heavy fall of rain.

clue.text: Oil source exhausted? How clever of you!

definitions.meaning: an oil field drilled until it is used up
praise for reasoning that has been carefully thought through

explanation.definitionFit: A drilling site has been spent, while a plan thought through is praised; both phrases fit.

clue.text: Component parts of a miscarriage of justice?

definitions.text: Component parts of a miscarriage of justice?

parts.words: Component parts of a miscarriage of justice?
parts.note: a miscarriage of justice is a court hearing plus a mistake, so its two parts make the phrase for learning by mistakes

explanation.surface: A legal analyst dissects a wrongful conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means learning by experiment and correcting mistakes.

clue.text: Cover crumpled, even cut

indicators.note: crumpled means squashed out of shape, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A crumpled blanket, though trimmed level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumpled' looks like a description of the cover, but it signals the anagram of the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop something is to wrap or enclose it, a synonym of covering it.

clue.text: Agent in capital backing ruler

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the whole assembly is read in reverse
in places the agent inside the capital city

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
a rep (representative) is a sales agent

explanation.surface: A spy in the capital supports the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money, but it is a city; 'backing' turns the whole assembly round.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the sovereign of an empire, so a kind of ruler.

clue.text: City, very big, in eastern country

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size for very big people

explanation.surface: A huge city in an Asian nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link here, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a landlocked nation of Southeast Asia, so a country in the East.

clue.text: Go out with members of royal entourage

definitions.meaning: to woo someone, to date them
the assembled courtiers and household of a sovereign

explanation.definitionFit: To woo a partner and the royal household attending a monarch are both senses of this word.

clue.text: Greek character after fellow's cheese

indicators.note: after puts the Greek letter behind the fellow's abbreviation

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man's cheese follows his friend's.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a crumbly white brined cheese made in Greece from sheep or goat milk.

clue.text: What's afforded by easily portable torch?

definitions.text: What's afforded by easily portable torch?

parts.words: What's afforded by easily portable torch?
parts.note: a torch gives illumination, and a torch that is easy to carry weighs little

explanation.surface: Advertising copy for a handy pocket flashlight.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch provides illumination, and something easily carried is not heavy; the word means both.

clue.text: Quantities of water coming over vessel

indicators.note: coming over in a down clue means flipping upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pools are bodies of standing water

explanation.surface: Waves crash over a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a one-masted sailing ship, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Head accepting private investigator's view

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the investigator goes inside the head

parts.note: onion is slang for the head, as in 'off one's onion'
PI stands for private investigator

explanation.surface: A boss takes on a detective's assessment.
explanation.walkthrough: Using onion for head is old British slang, as in 'off one's onion' for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a personal view or belief held on a matter.

clue.text: Force, Italian one clad in form of mail

indicators.note: clad in means dressed in, so the Italian and the one go inside the other letters
form of means a new shape of the word that follows, its letters rearranged

parts.note: It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An armed band, one Italian among them wearing chain mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges the letters of 'mail'; 'clad in' places the Italian and the one inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a body of citizen soldiers, so a military force.

clue.text: Sauce boat for sale?

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
something put up is offered for sale, as in 'up for auction'

explanation.surface: A gravy boat is being sold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce boat' suggests a gravy boat, but the boat is a sailing vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ketchup is a tomato-based condiment, a familiar table sauce.

clue.text: I'm inapt when playing percussion instruments

indicators.note: playing here means fooling about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drummer admits to being poor at playing the kettledrums.
explanation.definitionFit: These are kettledrums, tuned drums of the orchestra's percussion section.

clue.text: Collage Dad's put up outside entrance, initially

parts.note: pa is Dad, and the 's is kept as S

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the word goes around the first letter
up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Father has hung a picture over the front door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PUT into TUP, which goes round E, the first letter of 'entrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A paste-up is a collage of material pasted onto a sheet, as in page layout.

clue.text: Thief's liable to return with "bread" about

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the bread goes round the turned word

parts.note: bread is used here for food in general, as in 'daily bread'

indicators.note: to return means to go back, so the word for liable is read in reverse

parts.note: apt means liable or inclined

explanation.surface: A robber is likely to come back with money around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' in quotes suggests slang for money, but here it means food in general.
explanation.definitionFit: A footpad was a highwayman on foot, a robber of travellers.

clue.text: Small speculation in Liechtenstein, say

parts.note: FL is the international vehicle code for Liechtenstein
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A little investment in a tiny Alpine principality.
explanation.walkthrough: A flutter is British slang for a small bet; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A modest wager or gamble is called a flutter in British usage.

clue.text: Horse from Portugal that is lacking in charm

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal
ie stands for id est, that is
bald means plain and unadorned, without grace

explanation.surface: A Portuguese horse that is not attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald is a horse with patches of black and white.

clue.text: Some broad, American lady

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A big American woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broad' looks like slang for a woman, but it is only cover for the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A titled or elderly woman can be called this, a synonym for lady.

clue.text: Children matter

definitions.meaning: a subject or point under discussion

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both one's offspring and a topic being debated.

clue.text: Drop rent

definitions.meaning: a drop of water from the eye

explanation.definitionFit: A teardrop is a drop of liquid, and a rip in fabric is also called a rent.

clue.text: Laundry was hot

parts.note: taken as written; that the two pieces run on together in the clue is a coincidence of this charade, not a hidden word
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: The washing was warm.
explanation.definitionFit: The weekly wash means the clothes laundered together.

clue.text: Document produced by Republican in intelligence

indicators.note: in places the party letter within the word for intelligence

parts.note: wit means mental sharpness

explanation.surface: A paper written by a clever Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal legal document issued by a court.

clue.text: Unconscious Indian prince almost engulfed by river

indicators.note: engulfed by means swallowed by, so the prince goes inside the river

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the prince's title loses its last letter

parts.note: a nawab is a Muslim ruler in India

explanation.surface: An Indian ruler, nearly drowned in the river, has passed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unconscious' suggests knocked out, but it means not aware; 'almost' drops the prince's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconscious can mean not aware of something, a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Road not to be negotiated in dangerous wind

indicators.note: negotiated in the sense of worked round or managed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A road that cannot be travelled in a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent whirling windstorm, a destructive wind.

clue.text: Crafty one with the grids, Phi is exuberant

indicators.note: crafty means cunning or artfully made, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A clever compiler called Phi, with his grids, is in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Phi is another setter of crosswords; I, THE GRIDS and PHI are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being high-spirited means lively and full of energy, a synonym of exuberant.
